patterns.note: The hero section features an asymmetrical, split-screen typography layout that dominates the initial viewport, creating a strong visual statement before content is revealed.
Extremely large, thin, and widely spaced uppercase sans-serif typography is used for the main hero statement, contrasting with smaller, regular-weight sans-serif for navigation and body text.
A high-contrast color scheme is employed, primarily using a dark, almost black background with light text and a soft, desaturated pink as a key accent color revealed on scroll.
The oversized hero text scrolls out of view with a subtle parallax effect, while a light pink background simultaneously animates in from the top, transitioning the page to the main content grid.
Content is presented in distinct, full-width sections that replace each other as the user scrolls, rather than stacking, giving a sense of sequential discovery.

technique_notes: The hero section utilizes a scroll-triggered animation system, potentially leveraging canvas or Lottie as hinted, to create a dramatic parallax effect where large text elements move out of the viewport while a new background color animates in. This transition reveals the subsequent content section, which is a full-width grid of images.
The site employs a full-bleed image grid for its portfolio, where each image acts as a distinct content block, creating a visually rich and immersive showcase.

design_tokens.type_scale: Oversized, thin hero text (~5-6x body size) with small, understated navigation and body text, creating a dramatic visual hierarchy.
design_tokens.radius: Sharp corners throughout, with no visible rounding on any elements.
design_tokens.spacing: Very airy in the hero section, emphasizing the large typography, transitioning to a balanced and dense grid layout for the portfolio content.

standout: The site's most distinctive feature is its dramatic, oversized, and split-screen hero typography that dynamically scrolls out of view to reveal a curated, full-width image grid. This creates an immediate, art-gallery-like impression that prioritizes visual impact and a sense of discovery over immediate information delivery.
